title: Technicolor at the Nanoscale is Heating Up: How Monochromation and Liquid He/N2 Cryogenic Holders are Revolutionizing STEM
content: Thanks to aberration correction [1-3] in scanning/transmission electron microscopy (STEM), we now take for granted that imaging allows us to know where all the atoms are, and that electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) tells us what electrons do in terms of materials properties. However, until very recently, our view of materials has been in grayscale. Just as the advent of Technicolor transformed cinema by revealing a world of once-hidden hues, monochromation in STEM [4] is introducing new colors to our characterization toolbox—revolutionizing how we study materials at the atomic scale.
